Cluster ASVs using Swarm or VSEARCH

Source: R/cluster_fun.R
cluster_asv.Rd

This function clusters ASVs into molecular operational taxonomic units (mOTUs) or performs denoising depending on the chosen method and parameters. When using Swarm with d = 1, the result is equivalent to denoising.

Usage

cluster_asv(
  read_count,
  group = TRUE,
  by_sample = FALSE,
  method = "swarm",
  swarm_path = NULL,
  vsearch_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  swarm_d = 1,
  fastidious = FALSE,
  identity = 0.97,
  outfile = "",
  sep = ",",
  quiet = T,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

read_count

Data frame or CSV file containing the following columns: asv, sample, replicate (optional), read_count.

group

Logical; if TRUE, ASVs in the same cluster are aggregated into a single row. If FALSE, the input data frame is returned with an added cluster_id column.

by_sample

Logical: if TRUE, clustering is performed separately for each sample.

method

Character string specifying the clustering method: "swarm" or "vsearch".

swarm_path

Optional path to the swarm executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.swarm_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

vsearch_path

Optional path to the vsearch executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.vsearch_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Positive integer: number of CPUs to use. If 0, all available CPUs are used.

swarm_d

Positive integer: Swarm d parameter (maximum number of differences allowed between ASVs to cluster them together).

fastidious

Logical: if TRUE and swarm_d = 1, performs an additional clustering pass to reduce small clusters.

identity

Numeric value between 0 and 1. Identity threshold used for VSEARCH cluster_size clustering.

outfile

Character string: name of the output CSV file. If empty, no file is written.

sep

Field separator character used in input and output CSV files.

quiet

Logical: if TRUE, suppress informational messages and display only warnings or errors.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

A data frame. If group = TRUE, ASVs are merged by cluster; otherwise, the original structure is preserved with an additional cluster_id column.

Details

The function can use either Swarm or VSEARCH (cluster_size) to cluster ASVs in the input data set. Each ASV is assigned to a cluster, and the output format depends on the group argument.

Two output modes are available:

  • group = TRUE: ASVs belonging to the same cluster are merged into a single row. The asv_id and asv columns correspond to the cluster centroid, and read counts are summed across all ASVs in the cluster for each sample (and replicate, if present).

  • group = FALSE: The original data frame is returned with an additional cluster_id column. Each row corresponds to an individual ASV.

Clustering can be performed globally or independently for each sample using the by_sample argument.

Note: when by_sample = TRUE and group = FALSE, the same asv_id may be assigned different cluster_id values across samples.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
read_count_df <- cluster_asv(
  read_count = read_count_df,
  group = TRUE,
  method = "vsearch",
  by_sample = TRUE,
  num_threads = 4
)
} # }
